text:
Filip Chytil came back from injured reserve on Friday and, fittingly, his first game back was against the Rangers, the team that drafted him and traded him to Vancouver. It ended in a Canucks loss, and he's still looking for his first goal of the season.

That's the story of his time in Vancouver so far: talent, minutes and not enough healthy games. He played 12 games for the Canucks last season and eight this year, with two assists, both in the first two games, then six straight without a point. The five-on-five numbers are rough. Vancouver has taken only 25% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, though eight games is a tiny sample and Evolving-Hockey noted last season that he was stuck with some of the weakest linemates in the league.

Head coach Manny Malhotra has been giving him nearly 20 minutes a night, more than he usually gets. That's trust. What we'd watch now is simple: whether he stays in the lineup long enough for the shooting and the line combinations to settle into something real.
